“The Amicus”

Abstract

An archtop stringed instrument on outline C-75. Faceted Port Orford cedar top; rim cut whole from one alder blank; arched bigleaf maple back; one pickup hung from the fingerboard. The disclosure relates generally to music, and specifically to this.

Claims

What is claimed is:

  1. A stringed instrument comprising a rim (14) cut whole from a single blank, a carved top (10), an arched back (12), a set neck (40), a floating bridge (20) and a trapeze tailpiece (22).
  2. The instrument of claim 1, the top carved as seventeen (17) flat facets, each fold eased inside to a 25 mm radius, each ridge left crisp.
  3. The instrument of claim 2, the top graduated from 2.8 mm at the plateau to 3.2 mm at the skirt, the bridge base sitting flat on a hexagonal plateau.
  4. The instrument of claim 2, having two lipped soundholes in the side facets, the air within resonating at about 127 Hz.
  5. The instrument of claim 1, the top braced by a ring beam, two scalloped tone bars and one cross bar.
  6. The instrument of claim 1, the back arched in thirteen (13) facets, glued to a ledge routed in the rim, and unbraced.
  7. The instrument of claim 1, 2.0 deep at the edge, as Case No. C-75, the remaining depth being arch.
  8. The instrument of claim 1, the neck tenon dropping through a notch in the top, such that the neck is fitted last.
  9. The instrument of claim 1, having one pickup (24) hung from a bracket (26) beneath a floating fingerboard extension (42), no pickguard being present.
  10. The instrument of claim 2, the top dyed under shellac, a 1/4 in band at the edge left undyed, constituting binding obtained by the omission of dye.

Conditions of use

Form JPI-75A
The INSTRUMENT is to be operated by hand. Other methods of operation have not been evaluated.
  1. For use outside BILLABLE HOURS.
  2. The pickup (24) is active. Supply 9 V at the battery door (32). No tools are required.
  3. With the battery exhausted, the INSTRUMENT continues to produce output acoustically. This output is not metered.
  4. The fingerboard extension (42) floats 15.3 mm above the top. Do not load it.
  5. Hours of operation are recorded as NON-BILLABLE. Entries to date: none.
Caution

Top (10). Do not press the facets to confirm that they are flat. They are flat.

Manufacture and custody

Procedure JPI-M-1A

Made by hands and machines in Portland, Oregon.

  1. Rim (14) cut whole from one 1-3/4 in alder blank, from the top face, in one setup.
  2. Top (10) carved in flat planes, graduated, braced and lipped.
  3. Back (12) carved in facets and glued to the ledge. No linings are kerfed.
  4. All parts cut on a 3-axis router in one or two setups.
  5. Neck (40) fitted last.
  6. On production, the serial is entered in the ledger. No entry has been made.
